Theorem 1 (Chapter 130)

Subject: proof theory | ID: 68186

Theorem

Let H be a Lebesgue space. Every orthogonal operator T in B(H) with operator norm less than 1 satisfies the Neumann series expansion.

Proof

Step 1. By the bounded spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{01300011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the bounded spectral family.

Step 2. By the transcendental spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{01300012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the transcendental spectral family.

Step 3. Applying the algebraic interpolation theorem to \(P_{01300013}\), we obtain the norm bound in the mixed Lebesgue scale for the appropriate exponents.

Conclusion. The result follows by combining Steps 1-3 through polynomial approximation and the compactness of the spectral family.
